decision_reason: This is the Hugo source for GSA's Office of the Chief Technology Officer website, not a reusable software product. The README provides local build/preview instructions, but the website consumes USWDS as a dependency rather than implementing a reusable federal service or tool. The root LICENSE only states U.S.-territory public-domain status; no worldwide grant was established. Reject for product identity, with license scope also unresolved.

government_provenance.note: The exact README says this repository is the website for the General Services Administration Office of the Chief Technology Officer and that it is published on cloud.gov Pages.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Hugo site, assets, and build/preview instructions using npm and a local CMS.

eligible_license.note: The actual license text only states that as a U.S. government work the project is public domain within the United States. It does not include a worldwide CC0 dedication or an OSI-approved license; no broader grant was established.

primary_evidence.note: The README explicitly identifies this as the GSA CTO website and says it uses USWDS. It is site content/theme/deployment source, not the reusable USWDS toolkit or an independent operational software product.

product_identity: Tech at GSA website (Hugo site and content source; uses USWDS, does not implement USWDS)
agency: General Services Administration, Office of the Chief Technology Officer
license: U.S.-only public-domain notice; worldwide license/dedication unresolved
status_note: GitHub shows last commit 2025-05-08. Rejected as a website implementation rather than an independent software product; no catalog entry should be created for this site source.

decision_reason: The assigned 18F URL now redirects to the canonical `uswds/uswds` repository for the same U.S. Web Design System, not to a separate product. The system is an active GSA TTS product with documented installation/use, current releases, and broad government adoption. Its license clearly dedicates GSA-authored code worldwide to CC0 and enumerates the limited third-party assets under Apache-2.0, OFL-1.1, MIT, or CC0. Admit only as the existing `uswds` catalog product; no new product identity.

government_provenance.note: The official USWDS page says it was created by 18F and USDS in 2015 and is a GSA Technology Transformation Services product maintained by the Digital Services Division.

public_source.note: The redirected canonical repository publicly provides reusable UI component source, styles, design tokens, package build/distribution, and developer installation guidance.

eligible_license.note: The LICENSE.md dedicates the rest of the GSA-authored work worldwide under CC0-1.0. It separately identifies inherited third-party files under Apache-2.0, OFL-1.1, MIT, or CC0, all eligible grants; no blanket license is claimed over those components.

primary_evidence.note: The official product page identifies the exact system, history, sponsor, support channel, and use by dozens of agencies/nearly 200 sites. Current documentation provides installation guidance and v3.14.0 download; current repository publishes releases and source.

product_identity: U.S. Web Design System (USWDS): reusable federal UI component library, design tokens, and style guidance
